sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in the Town of Tonawanda?
sections.html:
Most owners choose between a traditional listing, a sale without an agent, and a direct offer from a cash buyer. This page covers the Town of Tonawanda in Erie County, which includes the Village of Kenmore. The separate City of Tonawanda lies just to the north and follows its own local rules.

A listing suits a house that shows well and does not need much work. A direct sale suits an owner who wants speed, a house that needs repairs, or a situation such as an inherited home or a move for work. Before you decide, add up what each route nets you, since the lowest-effort path is not always the one that leaves the most money behind.

  • Agent listing: more exposure, more preparation, and a closing that depends on a buyer's lender.
  • For sale by owner: you set the price and handle showings, contracts and negotiation.
  • Cash purchase: no lender in the middle, and the buyer takes the house in its present state.

Whichever path you pick, the town has one local requirement that every seller should know about, covered below.

sections.h2: What is the Town of Tonawanda like?
sections.html:
The town is the northern inner-ring suburb of Buffalo, with an estimated 70,853 residents on July 1, 2025, and 33,965 households in the 2020 to 2024 survey, per the Census Bureau. It covers 18.7 square miles of land between the Niagara River on the west and Niagara Falls Boulevard (US 62) on the east.

The first settlers arrived around 1805 and the Erie Canal, finished in 1825, drove early growth. The town was set apart from the Town of Buffalo in 1836, Kenmore incorporated as a village in 1899, and most of the rest of the town filled in with suburban housing in the 1940s and 1950s. Population peaked at 107,282 in 1970 and has drifted down since, and much of the housing dates to that suburban build-out.

Getting around is easy for commuters. Interstate 190 runs along the western side, Interstate 290 (the Youngmann Expressway) cuts across to US 62, and state routes 324, 265, 266 and 384 serve the neighborhoods. Mean travel time to work is 20.6 minutes.

Neighborhood names buyers will recognize include Brighton, Kenilworth, Parkview, Sheridan Parkside, Green Acres and Old Town, along with Ellicott Creek Park and the Sheridan and Brighton Park golf courses.

sections.h2: How do Tonawanda home values and ownership compare?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in the town at $213,900. About 72.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median household income is $77,673, and 20.1 percent of residents are 65 or older.

This is a stable town. Ninety percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and owner costs run $1,494 a month with a mortgage and $662 without. A buyer will compare your house with other 1950s-era suburban homes, so condition and updates carry weight.

Schools matter to buyers. The town is mostly in the Kenmore-Tonawanda Union Free School District, with Kenmore West and Kenmore East as the two public high schools, while a portion falls in the Sweet Home Central School District. Check which district a particular address belongs to before you describe it in an ad.

sections.h2: What does the town require before a Tonawanda house can be sold?
sections.html:
Selling a property in the Town of Tonawanda requires a certificate of compliance for the storm water system. According to the town's I Want To page, the inspection generally covers the sump pump and its electric line, footing drains, yard drains and downspouts. The Building Department schedules it at (716) 877-8801.

Do this early. If the inspector finds a failed pump or a downspout tied into the wrong line, you want time to fix it before a buyer's closing date arrives. The same page says permit records from before 1965 were destroyed, so for older repairs you may have to rely on your own paperwork.

Two programs may also affect you. If the town's 0% Residential Rehabilitation loan secures a mortgage on your house, it comes due when title transfers. The town's First Time Homebuyer Program was permanently suspended as of March 31, 2025, so do not count on it as a way to help a buyer with closing costs.

sections.h2: When are Tonawanda property taxes due and how do you challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
The town assessor values 28,828 parcels in the Town of Tonawanda and Village of Kenmore, with a combined market value of $10.9 billion, according to the assessor's page. Taxable status date is March 1, the tentative roll is filed May 1, and the final roll is filed by July 1.

Tonawanda tax calendar for 2025/26 as published by the town assessor

Village of KenmoreJuly 3November 17.5% in July

Ask the receiver of taxes at the Town Clerk's office for the figures for your own bill, since rates and dates are reset each year.

  • Informal review: between February 1 and April 1, send proof of your home's market value to the assessor.
  • Grievance Day: the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027. File form RP-524, and a written complaint is enough if you cannot attend.
  • Small Claims Assessment Review: for an owner-occupied one, two or three-family home after a Board of Assessment Review decision. The filing fee is $30 and petitions are due by July 30.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and recent changes should Tonawanda sellers know about?
sections.html:
The assessor's page says owner-occupied houses qualify for STAR, but the State runs that program and the town cannot change a STAR record. Anyone who switched from the exemption to the STAR credit check should tell their mortgage lender so an escrow account is adjusted.

The town also lists senior, disability, veterans, firefighter and volunteer ambulance exemptions. As of July 2026 the town adopted the exemption for permanently and totally disabled veterans, which is a full property tax exemption. Applications go through the assessor and are due March 1, 2027. A buyer who qualifies can ask about it, so a seller of a house occupied by such a veteran should mention it to the buyer's side.

Taxes are paid at the Town Clerk's office or through the online portal, but partial payments can only be made in person on weekdays from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection before selling my house in the Town of Tonawanda?
faqs.a: Yes. The town requires a certificate of compliance for the storm water system before a sale. It generally covers the sump pump, footing drains, yard drains and downspouts, and the Building Department at (716) 877-8801 schedules it.

faqs.q: Is the Town of Tonawanda the same as the City of Tonawanda?
faqs.a: No. They are separate municipalities in different jurisdictions, and this page covers the town, which surrounds the Village of Kenmore. The city sits to the north along the canal and is a separate municipality.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to grieve my assessment here?
faqs.a: Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027. You file form RP-524 with the assessor, and a written complaint with evidence is accepted if you do not want a hearing.

faqs.q: Who pays New York's transfer tax in Tonawanda?
faqs.a: The seller does, at $2 per $500 of price, unless the contract says otherwise. The TP-584 return goes to the Erie County Clerk within 15 days after the deed is delivered, and the Clerk can quote the recording charges.

faqs.q: How fast can a cash sale close in the Town of Tonawanda?
faqs.a: It depends on the buyer and the title work, so get a closing date in writing. The storm water certificate and any unpaid tax balances are the usual items that decide whether a closing date holds.
